newsitem.title: UK: UK drug firms want European biotech directive soon.
newsitem.headline: UK drug firms want European biotech directive soon.

text.p: A British drugs industry lobby group on Tuesday urged the European parliament to accept a new directive governing patent protection to help boost development of new medicines.
The Association of the British Pharmaceutical Industry (ABPI) said it hoped the debate would no longer be "clouded" by ethical and environmental concerns.
"The worry we have, is that the issues can so quickly become clouded by inappropriate emotional comments," ABPI president Peter Read told Reuters.
"There are other areas where these discussions (on ethical and environmental matters) can take place without in some way inhibiting the progress of the directive," he added.
Read was interviewed at an ABPI conference on genetic medicines.

The European parliament threw out an earlier draft for the European Directive for the Legal Protection of Biotechnological Inventions in March 1995 amid worries over the ethical and environmental consequences of genetic manipulation, Read said.
A new proposal will be discussed in the European Parliament early next year.

"These coming weeks are absolutely important in the context of informing MEPs in a balanced and right way," Read said, warning "we will see a slowdown in the development of the work that is going on now" if the proposed directive is rejected.
He added uniform patent protection would be in the interest of both patients and the biotech industry, which is coping with "confusing and unequal" protection across Europe.
"Clarification on the biotechnology directive is absolutely crucial for the continuation of the research development that is going on in Europe," Read said.
